title: Heterogeneous canary mesh + policy-driven promotion for LTS & rolling upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: Our current progressive delivery tooling treats canaries as homogeneous cohorts and uses single-metric gates (error-rate or latency). This misses cross-cutting regressions that only appear in specific combinations of model variant, GPU class (A100 vs H100), and region. We need a promotion system that supports a heterogeneous canary mesh (multiple orthogonal cohort axes), policy-driven promotion rules tied to LTS channels, and deterministic auto-rollback when a multi-signal adjudicator detects regressions. Goal: enable safe, repeatable promotions from canary -> staged -> LTS channels with minimal manual intervention and clear audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Define and implement a policy DSL to express weighted promotions across axes (region, hw-class, model-variant, customer-segment)
Implement heterogeneous canary mesh evaluation that runs per-axis checks and a global adjudicator that combines signals
Integrate rollback actions with existing traffic-router to divert traffic to compatible fallback variants within 60s of adjudicated failure
Expose per-promotion audit trail in Console: who triggered, policy used, metrics snapshot, and auto-rollback reason
Run 3 staging simulations on synthetic traffic with zero customer-impact and document outcomes
tasks: Design policy DSL and validation schema (PRD + examples)
Implement admission controller for promotion plans in control-plane (API + storage)
Extend telemetry pipeline to compute cohort-level SLI deltas and hallucination regression signals
Build adjudicator service that ingests cohort SLIs and outputs promote/halt/rollback decisions
Wire auto-rollback to routing layer and add safe-backoff schedule
Console UX: Promotion editor and audit timeline view
Create runbook for manual intervention and postmortem templates
rollout_plan: Phase A (week 1): deploy adjudicator behind feature flag to control plane and run shadow promotions against canary traffic only. Phase B (week 2): enable routing automation for <1% of production traffic split across orthogonal axes (region, hw-class). Phase C (week 3): expand to 10% with automatic halt on SLO breach and manual approval to advance to staged. Phase D: staged -> LTS promotion gated by a sustained absence of regressions for 72h and stakeholder approval. Each phase includes a dry-run window and mandatory simulation run.
telemetry_sli_slo: Primary SLIs: p95 latency (ms), client-visible errors (5xx + model-level errors), hallucination regression (eval-set false-positive rate), throughput. SLO thresholds: p95 <= baseline + 20%, error-rate < baseline + 0.5%, hallucination delta < 0.2ppt. Adjudicator computes z-score across cohorts and flags deviations > 3 sigma for automatic rollback consideration.
notes: Trade-offs: A mesh increases operational complexity but catches multidimensional regressions that single-cohort canaries miss.
Decision: start with conservative promotion weights and conservative SLI thresholds to reduce false-positive rollbacks.
Risk: telemetry latency (pipeline window) could delay rollback. Mitigation: add fast-path short-window SLIs (1m) for critical errors and router-level circuit-breakers.
Review feedback 2026-02-22 (PM): ensure promotion policy can be parameterized per-customer for enterprise contracts.
Follow-up: coordinate with Dedicated team to ensure reserved capacity can be reserved for rollback variants during promotions.
